body: By the way, if we actually need this to be about bytes, my recommendation would be always UTF-8 and UTF-8 encode. If we can somehow deal with a response containing a JavaScript string, we could just match Chrome/WebKit. (Possible, but probably ugly. Much better to require UTF-8 encode I think.)

Issues filed for `target` attribute not working:

* https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=749492
* https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=174891

Some updates on the Blink front. After @natechapin's https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/9d459e0a200786c290cc3beb47d676e52a94d243 (scheduled for [Chrome 77](https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/commit/9d459e0a200786c290cc3beb47d676e52a94d243)), Chrome now always does UTF-8 encoding/decoding for javascript URLs rather than using the JavaScript string directly, which is the [best case scenario](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1129#issuecomment-318080580). So the last test case (unpaired surrogates) in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1129#issuecomment-318068941 now fails. Additionally, the `window-1252` case has been failing for a while now (at least since Chrome 75) as Chrome has been forcing UTF-8 charset on the resulting document.

Additionally, the `<a>` tests in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1129#issuecomment-318068941 now run in Chrome, as they fixed [the `target` bug](https://crbug.com/749492) in Chrome 76. However, in 77 because they started doing UTF-8 encoding/decoding, the very last test case (unpaired surrogates) also started failing.

So it looks like @annevk's tests were committed to WPT at some point, yay: [results](https://wpt.fyi/results/html/browsers/browsing-the-web/navigating-across-documents/javascript-url-return-value-handling-dynamic.html?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=javascript-url).

However I'm trying to spec this and I think I must be confused on the desired behavior for the `[0xDE0D,0x41]` test case.

If we spec the body as doing a UTF-8 encode of the JS string `'\uDE0D\u41'`, we get the bytes 0xEF 0xBF 0xBD 0x41, right?

But when you feed that body into a UTF-8 decoder, which is what I presume would happen (we'd force the charset to UTF-8 via Content-Type), then the result would be the JS string `'\uFFFDA'`. Right?

However Chrome seems to instead produce the JS string `'\uFFFD\uFFFD\uFFFDA'`.

Is my understanding correct?

@domenic This looks potentially like a Blink bug. When we set a breakpoint at [where UTF-16 JavaScript string is converted to UTF-8](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/bindings/core/v8/script_controller.cc;l=245;drc=c8812dc700365682463f113d0d6a13dd43835dc2), we can see that the converted result is actually ED B8 8D 41, where the unpaired surrogate is translated to UTF-8 directly without any checking. This is probably an artifact of [kLenientUTF8Conversion](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/wtf/text/string_utf8_adaptor.h;l=49;drc=c8812dc700365682463f113d0d6a13dd43835dc2), where kStrictUTF8ConversionReplacingUnpairedSurrogatesWithFFFD would do the right thing. Filed https://crbug.com/1221018.
